territorial_scope.description: Federal bill applying to persons deploying covered advanced AI systems for use in interstate or foreign commerce.

evidence.quote: No person may deploy an advanced artificial intelligence system for use in interstate or foreign commerce unless that person is in compliance with subsection (a).

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: If enacted, requires the Secretary of Energy to establish an Advanced AI Evaluation Program within 90 days; developers of AI systems trained with over 10^26 operations must participate and provide materials on request, and may not deploy without compliance, subject to fines of at least $1,000,000 per day.
summary.long: S. 2938, the Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025, introduced in the Senate on 29 September 2025 and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, would direct the Secretary of Energy to establish, within 90 days of enactment, an Advanced Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Program within the Department of Energy. The program would offer standardized and classified testing of advanced AI systems, including adversarial testing by red teams, to collect data on the likelihood of adverse AI incidents, and would provide participating entities with formal reports and recommended containment protocols. An advanced AI system is one trained with more than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations. The Secretary may propose a replacement definition by rule, which takes effect only after Congress enacts a joint resolution approving it. Covered advanced AI system developers must participate in the program and, on request, provide the Secretary with code, training data, model weights, and implementation and training information. No person may deploy such a system for use in interstate or foreign commerce unless compliant. Violators are fined not less than $1,000,000 per day of violation. The Secretary must submit a plan for a permanent federal oversight framework within 360 days and update it annually. The program terminates seven years after enactment unless renewed by Congress.

notes: Bill text as introduced 29 Sep 2025. The text states no amendments, repeals, implementing or legal-basis relations. Reader notes: (1) 'deploy' is defined (Sec. 3(8)) as an action taken by a covered advanced AI system developer, while the Sec. 4(b) prohibition says 'No person may deploy'; the reach of the prohibition to non-developers is unclear. (2) The Sec. 4 heading refers to enforcement, but the text names no enforcing authority or procedure and states no maximum penalty; Sec. 4(c) sets a minimum fine of $1,000,000 per day. (3) Sec. 3(1)(B) lets the Secretary propose an alternative advanced AI definition, which takes effect only after a joint resolution is enacted. (4) Timing: program within 90 days (Sec. 5(a)), plan within 360 days (Sec. 5(c)(1)), annual updates (Sec. 5(c)(3)), sunset after 7 years unless renewed (Sec. 5(d)).
